title: RLHF with PPO vs DPO
subtitle: Both start from the SFT model and the same preference data: (prompt, chosen, rejected) triples ranked by humans. They differ in whether a reward model sits in the middle.

panels.label: RLHF · PPO
panels.key: Train a reward model, then optimise against it
flow: **SFT model**: base model fine-tuned on instructions
**Preference data**: sample 2+ responses, humans rank them
**Reward model**: SFT + scalar head, trained so score(chosen) > score(rejected)
**PPO**: the policy samples, the RM scores, the KL penalty holds it near SFT

panels.label: DPO
panels.key: Skip the reward model; optimise the policy directly
flow: **Same SFT model**, frozen as the reference π_ref
**Same preference triples**: chosen y_w, rejected y_l
**No reward model**: the optimal policy has a closed form
**One loss**: widen the margin between chosen and rejected, relative to π_ref

callout.label: Both keep a KL anchor.
callout.text: Without it the policy **reward-hacks**: it finds responses that score high but are unlike natural language, and forgets its original language capabilities. In DPO, β sets that strength (typical 0.1–0.5).
